prompt:
The weekly order report in src/ gives wrong totals. Symptoms we have seen:

- An order placed on a Sunday is counted in the following week instead of the week that is ending.
- On our servers, which run in US Pacific time, orders placed shortly before or after midnight UTC on a week boundary land in the wrong week, and the week labels are sometimes a day off. In UTC the labels look right.
- Calling weeklyTotals twice in the same process gives a second answer that includes the orders of the first call.
- weeklyTotalsFor and recentWeeks show the same kind of wrong weeks.
- monthlyTotals, startOfMonth and daysInMonth (src/month.mjs) put orders in the wrong month, or give the wrong number of days, around the end of a month in some time zones.
- weekNumber and weekRangeLabel (src/labels.mjs) are off by one around the new year and in other time zones.
- Orders whose `placedAt` has no Z and no offset (for example 2024-03-10T22:30:00) are placed in different weeks depending on the server time zone.

The rules the report must follow:

1. A week starts on Monday at 00:00:00.000 UTC and ends before the next Monday 00:00:00.000 UTC. An order belongs to the week that contains its UTC instant, whatever offset its `placedAt` text carries (for example 2024-03-10T22:30:00-05:00 is 2024-03-11T03:30Z).
2. A week is labeled with the UTC date of its Monday as YYYY-MM-DD.
3. Every function in src/dates.mjs, src/range.mjs, src/report.mjs, src/month.mjs and src/labels.mjs must give the same answer in every process time zone, including around daylight saving changes and the new year.
4. `weeklyTotals` returns rows { week, orders, total } sorted by week ascending, and each call depends only on the orders passed to it.

5. A `placedAt` or other timestamp text with no Z and no offset is read as UTC (`2024-03-10T22:30:00`, `2024-03-10T22:30`, `2024-03-10T22:30:15.250` and a date alone such as `2024-03-10`). `parseTimestamp` still throws an Error whose message starts with `invalid timestamp` for text that is not a date.
6. Months are UTC calendar months. `startOfMonth(date)` returns midnight UTC of the first day of the month of `date`. `daysInMonth(date)` returns the number of days of that month (leap years included). `monthlyTotals(orders)` returns rows { month, orders, total } with `month` as YYYY-MM, sorted by month ascending, and depends only on the orders passed to it.
7. `weekNumber(date)` returns the ISO 8601 week of the UTC day of `date` as `YYYY-Www` (two digit week, week based year): weeks start on Monday and week 1 is the week that contains January 4, so 2024-12-30 is `2025-W01`, 2021-01-03 is `2020-W53` and 2024-03-10T23:30:00Z is `2024-W10`.
8. `weekRangeLabel(weekKey)` takes the YYYY-MM-DD of a Monday and returns the label of that week from Monday to Sunday with English month abbreviations (Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec), a space, a hyphen and a space between the two days: `Mar 4 - Mar 10, 2024`, `Feb 26 - Mar 3, 2024`, and when the week spans two years `Dec 30, 2024 - Jan 5, 2025`. Text that is not the date of a real Monday in exactly the form YYYY-MM-DD (including a Tuesday, `2024-02-30` or an empty string) throws an Error with the message `invalid week: <text>`.
9. No helper changes the Date objects it is given.

Find the causes and fix them. Keep the existing file names and exports. The tests in test/ only cover the report; add tests of your own for the date, month and label helpers, and make sure `npm test` passes. You can try other time zones by setting the TZ environment variable, for example `TZ=America/Los_Angeles npm test`.
